testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: Under the `speed` Objective, when the group's speed-row Cell is one of the cost row's exploration Cells (e.g. cost task-high, speed task-xhigh), `assignment_prob` is wrong for that Cell: an exploring Pull that draws the policy Cell records 1/20 and a non-exploring Pull records 4/5, though the Cell's real assignment probability is 4/5 + 1/(5K) = 17/20. The ticket requires 'the probability that the Cell it actually runs was assigned to it'.
survived.evidence: In the copy I ran `node probe-speed.mjs`. Its table has rows cost:{*:task-high}, speed:{*:task-xhigh} and the fixed test install; it calls route() for tickets 1..400 with implRow 5 and 3, objective speed. Output: `pool { by: 'every-5th', cells: [ 'task-xhigh', 'task-medium', 'slow-medium', 'smol-xhigh' ] }` and `{ 'explore policy=task-xhigh chosen=task-xhigh prob=1/20': 113, 'stay policy=task-xhigh chosen=task-xhigh prob=4/5': 400, 'explore ... chosen=slow-medium prob=1/20': 100, ... }`. The same Cell gets two different recorded probabilities, and neither is its marginal probability. A tripped speed row has the same defect, because it falls back to slow-high, which is in the pool when the cost Cell is task-xhigh or slow-xhigh. The test fixture rowTable never puts the speed Cell in the cost Cell's exploration set, so the suite cannot catch this.
survived.suggested_fix: Two options. (1) Exclude the Pull's own policy Cell from the draw cells when the objective is not cost, and use that K. (2) Have assignmentProb take `cell`, `policy` and `cells`: return 4/5 + 1/(5K) when cell === policy and policy ∈ cells, 1/(5K) for any other drawn cell, and 4/5 otherwise. Add a route test with speed≠cost rows whose speed Cell is a cost exploration Cell.

votes.reason: I did not run a probe or the suite, so this verdict rests on reading the snapshot code only. In `route` (ticket-router.mjs ~L600-630), the policy Cell comes from `dispatch(objective)` and the exploration pool from `dispatch("cost").draw.cells`. The draw is `drawCell` with `policyCell: null`, and the comment says the pool never holds the group's own Cell, which only covers the cost row's Cell. `assignmentProb` receives only `{burnIn, chainHead, exploring, K}`. It returns 1/(5K) for an exploring Pull and 4/5 otherwise, and has no input saying whether the speed policy Cell is in the draw pool. So when the speed Cell is one of the cost row's exploration Cells, an exploring Pull that draws it records 1/20 and a non-exploring Pull records 4/5. The true marginal is 4/5 + 1/(5K), which is 17/20 for K=4. The claim as described holds in the code. I did not check the tripped-speed-row case. The doc comment says a Pull "runs its group's Cell at the share left", which matches the code but not the ticket's wording. CWD-AUDIT: not run; I changed no files and created none under /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin.

Not refuted, by code reading only: I did not run the probe. At ticket-router.mjs:458 and :614 the pool is explorationCells(centre = the cost-row Cell, ...) filtered to Cells the install defines and the guard hasn't tripped. It excludes only the cost Cell. The policy Cell comes from the objective's row, so a speed Cell that is one of the cost Cell's exploration Cells stays in the pool. Line 546 then computes assignmentProb from K = pool size alone. That gives 1/(5K) on an exploring Pull and 4/5 on a non-exploring Pull, whichever Cell was drawn. The Cell's true marginal in the overlap case is 4/5 + 1/(5K). Lens 2, handled elsewhere: nothing handles it. No other code adjusts for the overlap, and pull.md:291 and CONTEXT.md:574 describe '4/5 at the group's Cell, 1/5 of 1 over the Cells drawn', which is exactly this behavior. The docs therefore document the defect and do not resolve it. Narrowing: it only matters when the objective row's Cell differs from the cost Cell and lies in its exploration set; in burn-in, or when the cost and objective rows agree, the recorded value is correct. The claim's 'neither is its marginal' is accurate. survived.evidence: probe.mjs through the CLI at --impl-row 5, table past burn-in, guard ok. Healthy install: `CELL=slow-xhigh DRAW=2/3 BY=every-5th ... REASON=ok`, prob=1/15. REASON=ok`, assignment_prob=1, exploration_draw="". Only a throw (bad JSON, missing file, omp absent) reaches the WARNING branch. readOmpJson validates only that the top level is an object. `readOmpConfigValue` returns `.value`, so an omp reply of `{}` gives `undefined`, which resolveRole turns into [] with no signal. `installOf` itself does the silent flattening (`catalogEntry(...)?.thinking`, `Array.isArray(thinking) ? ... : []`).
survived.suggested_fix: Have installOf (or main) refuse a modelRoles that is not an object and a catalog without a `models` array, which tier-roles' checkRoutes already does via kindOf, so the existing catch warns. Also warn when the Pull is past burn-in, may explore, and every ladder is empty or `defined` ends up with no Cell the group could use. Do not let that case pass as a plain `REASON=ok`.

refuted.claim: When the install read fails (the loud-looking WARNING path), the failure reaches stderr only: the Routing line / ledger `## Routed` entry still says REASON=ok, and the ticket-features row records assignment_prob=1. On a non-exploring Pull that probability is false. Past burn-in a normal Pull runs its group's Cell at 4/5, but the failed read leaves `install` null, `drawRow.draw` becomes null, and assignmentProb takes the K===0 branch.
refuted.evidence: probe.mjs `bad json roles, NON-exploring row3`: stderr has the WARNING, but stdout is `... DRAW=- BY=- ... REASON=ok` and prob=1. The healthy row 3 run gives prob=4/5. probe2.mjs with PATH=/nonexistent: exit 0, WARNING `omp config get modelRoles --json failed: spawnSync omp ENOENT`, stdout `... REASON=ok`. The new test 'an install it cannot read warns...' asserts the same prob "1" and so pins it. Nothing in the committed ledger/features data marks the row as degraded. ROUTING_REASONS has no value for it, and `degrade()` is never called for it.
refuted.suggested_fix: Make a failed install read degrade the Routing REASON (a new ROUTING_REASONS value, or route()'s `degrade`) so the ledger shows it. Record assignment_prob blank (unknown, which the column already defines) instead of "1" for a Pull whose exploration pool could not be determined. Do not let it feed the Fit as certain.

votes.reason: I read the code and did not run it. The mechanics match the claim. A failed install read leaves install null, so K=0 and assignmentProb returns "1" (ticket-router.mjs:547). On a failed read no exploration draw happens, so the Cell is assigned deterministically and 1 is the true propensity of that run. The doc comment says K=0 means "the Pull's Cell was certain", and the WARNING says "no exploration Cell is drawn". What remains is the missing degraded marker in REASON, a design gap rather than a false value. Given the instruction to refute when uncertain, I refute. No red/green run was made; the check was reading the code only. CWD-AUDIT: not run (I made no writes; cwd /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin).

The only signal of the failure is the stderr WARNING at ticket-router.mjs:1053. That branch calls neither `degrade()` nor any reason code, so `reason` falls through to "ok". The doc comment at line 541 describes K=0 as 'no draw, certain', so the "1" is partly by design. But on a non-exploring Pull the install read does not affect which Cell runs, so recording "1" rather than 4/5 is still wrong. unverified.claim: Every non-chain-head `route` past burn-in now spawns `omp` twice, including the 4-in-5 Pulls that do not explore. That adds about 5.7 s per Pull on this host, through execFileSync with no timeout, and pull.mjs stage_route also spawns the router with no timeoutMs. A hung omp therefore hangs the Pull. The shipped router-table.json has `"burn_in": false`, so this applies on every install now.

I did not reproduce a hang.

unverified.claim: assignmentProb takes `{burnIn, chainHead, exploring, K}` as a loose boolean bag. Combinations that cannot occur are representable, and the branch order resolves them silently (past burn-in, chainHead && exploring returns '1' ahead of the exploring branch). The 'blank means unknown, never 1 or 0' invariant is also unenforced on the writer, because `1` is returned for both a certain Cell and the read-failure fallback.
unverified.evidence: Read the diff of assignmentProb and route(): `exploring = table.burn_in || (implRow % EXPLORE_EVERY === 0 && !chainHead)`. That makes (burnIn=false, chainHead=true, exploring=true) unreachable from route, yet the function accepts it. The unit test calls it directly with burn-in chain-head and exploring=true. An install-read failure (install=null, so K=0) writes '1' with only the stderr warning as a trace.
unverified.suggested_fix: Pass a single `mode` ('burn-in' | 'chain-head' | 'explore' | 'policy') instead of three booleans. Consider whether a failed install read should write blank (unknown) rather than a certain '1'.

unverified.claim: `install = null` is a default parameter on rowDispatch/route, so a caller that forgets to pass the install silently gets 'no exploration Cell' after burn-in. The sentinel means both 'not read' and 'read failed', and only the test files pass it explicitly.
